title: German Umweltzone fine: what happens if you drive without a green sticker
description: Enter a German low-emission zone without a green Umweltplakette and you're looking at a €100 fine. Here's how enforcement actually works.
excerpt: No sticker in an Umweltzone means a €100 fine. Here's what enforcement really looks like — and whether the ticket follows you home.
content:
Every low-emission zone (Umweltzone) in Germany requires a valid green Umweltplakette stuck to your windshield. Driving in without one is a flat **€100 fine** — and no, the officer won't waive it just because your car would technically qualify. The check only looks at what's on the glass.

## How the check actually works

Two kinds of patrols: foot officers in city centres (Berlin, Munich and Stuttgart are the most active) and mobile car patrols cruising residential streets and parking lots. They don't stop every car, but foreign plates — Czech, Polish, Austrian — get flagged fast because they statistically miss the sticker most often. The check itself takes 30 seconds: look at the windshield, note the plate, print a ticket. You don't pay on the spot — the notice arrives by mail in 2–3 weeks.

## Do fines cross the border?

Yes, reliably. Germany has cross-border enforcement treaties with most EU countries for traffic fines over €70. The notice arrives translated, through your local police or directly. Ignore it and next time you enter Germany they can flag your plate and block the car until you pay.

## "I bought one, just forgot to stick it on"

Doesn't count. The sticker has to be physically on the windshield, visible from the driver's side. "I have one at home" costs the same €100 as "I don't have one". Get it from [nemeckaplaketa.cz](https://nemeckaplaketa.cz) and stick it on the moment it arrives.
